about.introTitle: Thoughtful tools for everyday cooking, born from quiet kitchens and generational timber.
about.introDescription: Founded in 2021 by culinary designer Eleanor Vance, Ladle & Co. is an enduring protest against synthetic gadgets. We cultivate slow-crafted, heirloom-grade kitchenware meant to live gracefully on open shelves and gather memories over generations.
about.workshopImageAlt: Sunlit Tuscan woodworker workshop with olivewood tools
about.workshopDescription: Every carved groove begins with salvaged Umbrian rootwood, shaped by hand to honor natural grain contours rather than mechanical symmetry.
about.oliveOilImageAlt: Olive oil poured from an artisan ceramic cruet
about.finishTitle: Finished purely with wild Apennine beeswax and organic cold-pressed citrus extracts.
about.finishDescription: Your food only touches clean, unvarnished natural fibers that age deeper and warmer every single day.
about.manifestoTitle: Three commitments to honest living and patient culinary rituals.
about.honestMaterialsDescription: We exclusively harvest single-block ancient olivewood pruned responsibly from regenerative Italian groves. Paired with lead-free unglazed clay stoneware and untreated solid brass that naturally patinas with touch and memory.
about.slowCraftsmanshipDescription: Air-cured timber resting for six patient months through seasonal humidity cycles. No synthetic microwave kilns, no polyurethane glazes. Our pieces are hand-rubbed with botanical waxes to let the wood breathe freely.
about.lifetimeUtilityDescription: Designed as durable companions, not disposable conveniences. Balanced ergonomic handles that fit the palm naturally, ready to accompany decades of simmered ragù, hearty sourdough kneading, and festive holiday tables.
about.founderImageAlt: Eleanor Vance, Founder of Ladle & Co.
about.founderQuote: The kitchen is not a laboratory of cold efficiency. It is the sensory heart of human shelter—a sanctuary of steam, fragrance, and conversation where memory is seasoned with everyday wood and fire.
about.founderDescription: After ten years as an architectural designer, Eleanor sought kitchen tools that shared the permanence and grace of mid-century furniture. When modern retailers offered only fragile plastics and chemical veneers, she moved to Umbria to apprentice with an elder woodturner, establishing what would quickly become the foundation of Ladle & Co.
about.guildDescription: We do not own remote industrial factories. We collaborate directly with sovereign artisan cooperatives, paying 35% above fair-wage benchmarks.
about.rossiGuildDescription: Specializing in single-piece ladles, stirring paddles, and grain-matched tasting spoons using non-bearing regional olive timber.
about.rossiGuildImageAlt: Italian wood turner working in a Tuscan workshop
about.katoGuildDescription: Fourteenth-generation stoneware ceramics, unglazed mortar & pestle sets, and heat-retaining utensil storage crocks.
about.katoGuildImageAlt: Japanese ceramic artisan shaping stoneware clay
about.ferreiroGuildDescription: Hand-riveted solid brass fittings, measuring cups, and dough scrapers hand-hammered for tactile kitchen responsiveness.
about.ferreiroGuildImageAlt: Portuguese metalsmith shaping brass cookware tools
about.sourcingTitle: From Tuscan hill to culinary table
about.sourcingDescription: Each utensil takes seven months to complete, letting natural moisture balance naturally to prevent cracks or warping over a lifetime.
about.ethicalHarvestDescription: Only pruned branches from non-bearing century groves are gathered during late autumn dormancy, leaving living trees intact.
about.tuscanSeasoningDescription: Rough timber logs rest in covered, breezy outdoor sheds across changing humidity cycles to gently stabilize natural cell walls.
about.latheChiselDescription: Turned by third-generation woodturners, then finished using Japanese hand-rasps for soft contours tailored to the palm.
about.organicWaxDipDescription: Submerged in warm local organic beeswax and cold-pressed orange peel oil to nourish, seal, and highlight the golden marble grain.
about.plasticFreePackagingDescription: Recycled unbleached kraft paper & soy inks
about.heirloomWarrantyDescription: Free replacement or repair against splitting
about.careTitle: Wood loves olive oil as much as your pasta does.
about.careDescription: Never place raw timber in a mechanical dishwasher. Simply rinse with tepid water and mild plant soap, dry immediately with linen, and massage with a drop of olive oil every full moon.

about.ctaDescription: Explore our seasonal drop of carved olivewood, hand-thrown ceramics, and hand-finished culinary companions.
